analytic_results: Two-dimensional continuum curvature maximum principle and exact energy dissipation on any smooth existence interval.
Existing DeTurck cutoffs: quantitative vanishing energy allowance and local full-sequence energy/dissipation convergence.
Distinct projected Yang--Mills gradient model: exact energy dissipation, all-time existence for each finite cutoff, and a cutoff-independent L2 excursion bound.
Armijo Euler line search terminates for nonstationary states and decreases energy for each accepted step in exact arithmetic.
formalization: 15 supporting theorems; no complete PDE maximum-principle, Fourier integration, or global finite-ODE existence formalization claimed.
limitations: Global finite-cutoff existence is not a global continuum-limit theorem.
The new projected-gradient ODE differs from the previously analyzed DeTurck cutoffs.
No locally gauge-equivariant finite spectral evolution or local Wilson lattice flow is claimed.
Numerical integration and acceptance checks use ordinary floating point, not certified intervals.
